clue.text: Musical sergeant returning cap for sprinkler

parts.note: Sgt Pepper, from the Beatles album Sgt Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band

indicators.note: returning means the word for the cap is read backwards

parts.note: a cap or lid is a top

explanation.surface: A sergeant in a musical swaps his cap for a garden sprinkler.
explanation.definitionFit: A pepper pot is a shaker that sprinkles ground pepper over food, so it is a kind of sprinkler.

clue.text: Poles originally transported in river vessel

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: in says that letter goes inside the vessel

parts.note: SS is a steamship

indicators.note: originally takes the opening letter of transported

explanation.surface: Polish people first carried in a river boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles looks like people from Poland; it means stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Posts are upright stakes or columns, just as poles are.

clue.text: Struggling in art, be poor apprentice

indicators.note: struggling means the letters writhe into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A trainee artist struggles at art school and is poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A probationer is a newcomer on trial, learning the job like an apprentice.

clue.text: Press chief penning note about poem in cipher

indicators.note: penning says the editor encloses the other pieces as in a pen

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the chief of a newspaper
C is circa, about
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor writes a note about a poem in secret code.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in cipher has been put into a secret code.

clue.text: Non-belligerent condition is enshrined in treaty

indicators.note: enshrined in says these words are set inside the treaty

parts.note: a pact is a treaty
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A peace treaty enshrines non-aggression as a term.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacifist refuses to fight or take part in war, so is non-belligerent.

clue.text: Initiation of this Italian test upset singer

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the whole run upside down
initiation of takes the starting letter of this

parts.note: the MOT is the annual UK roadworthiness test for vehicles

explanation.surface: An Italian exam is overturned at the very start.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomtit is a small songbird, a singer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Dumbo: Disney's brainchild initially bringing in little?

indicators.note: bringing in says the two opening letters take another piece between them
initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words Disney's and brainchild

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal for little

explanation.surface: Dumbo the flying elephant is presented as Walt Disney's own little idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Dumbo looks like the Disney elephant, but here it is a common noun for a dimwit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumbo is slang for a stupid person, and a dweeb is a dull, socially inept one.

clue.text: Ready overseas once to include companion in play

definitions.note: ready money abroad in former times, a past foreign currency unit

indicators.note: to include says the play encloses the companion

parts.note: a drama is a play
CH is a Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A companion is cast in a play that is ready to go abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready is cash, as in readies, not prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: The drachma was the currency of Greece before the euro, so it was foreign cash.

clue.text: Flightless bird originally eliciting letter from abroad

indicators.note: originally takes the opening letter of eliciting

parts.note: mu is a Greek letter

explanation.surface: A flightless bird prompts a letter from overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large Australian bird that cannot fly.

clue.text: Petty officer stole this empty wagon

parts.note: a boa is a feather or fur stole

indicators.note: empty leaves only the outside letters of this

parts.note: a wain is a farm wagon

explanation.surface: A petty officer stole an empty wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: Stole looks like a verb; it is a scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatswain is the ship's officer in charge of rigging and deck crew, a petty officer rank.

clue.text: Phlegmatic type's standing briefly recognised around India

indicators.note: around says the shortened word is placed round the letter for India
briefly means the word for standing is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: stock is standing or reputation, as in a man of good stock
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A calm person's reputation is acknowledged in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recognised' is a link word here, attached to the idea of acknowledged standing rather than giving letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic endures pain and hardship without complaint or show of feeling, which makes them a phlegmatic sort.

clue.text: Plant in holiday venue — ring-shaped, some say

parts.note: a holiday camp is a resort for holidaymakers

indicators.note: some say tells us the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: annular means shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A plant grows at a resort, laid out in a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Campanula is the bellflower genus, a garden plant with bell-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Distance of seafood outlet to west of loch

indicators.note: to west of in an across clue places the first piece to the left of the second

parts.note: a stand of fish is a stall selling seafood
Loch Ness is the famous Scottish loch

explanation.surface: How far a fish stall stands from a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Distance looks like a measurement but means aloofness here.
explanation.definitionFit: Distance in manner, keeping people at arm's length, is aloofness or coolness.

clue.text: Burden in French Canada at first, cooking cream bun

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of Canada
cooking means the letters are mixed up as in a recipe

explanation.surface: A cream bun cooked in French Canada weighs heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: An encumbrance is a load or impediment that weighs someone down.

clue.text: Infantile learner withdrawn from cool course

indicators.note: withdrawn from says the learner's letter is taken out of the word for cool

parts.note: to chill is to cool
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car
a dish is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: A childish student is taken off a fashionable course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantile behaviour is babyish and immature, as a young child's would be.

clue.text: Future monarch possibly has lyrics revised

indicators.note: revised means the letters are reworked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An heir to the throne rewrites some song lyrics.
explanation.walkthrough: Monarch is the butterfly, not a king or queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupa becomes an adult butterfly, so it may be a monarch butterfly in waiting.

clue.text: Part of shopfront, as cased by female spies?

indicators.note: cased by says the word as is held inside the other pieces like goods in a case

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: Female spies casing a shop before a raid examine its front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cased' plays on spies casing a joint, but it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascia is the board above a shop window that carries the shop's name.

clue.text: Drinking-place at hotel outside one French resort

indicators.note: outside says the bar lies around the numeral for one

parts.note: a bar is a drinking place
I is the Roman numeral one
the Ritz is a famous luxury hotel

explanation.surface: A bar at a hotel outside a single French seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Biarritz is a fashionable seaside town on the Bay of Biscay in south-west France.

clue.text: Celebrity from London won Eritreans over

indicators.note: over says those letters are then read backwards
from says the letters are taken from inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A star Eritrean team beats London.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity here is fame, the state of being widely known and acclaimed.

clue.text: Measure of power and income a non-drinker accepted

indicators.note: accepted says the income takes in the other pieces

parts.note: a wage is income
TT is teetotal, a non-drinker

explanation.surface: A teetotaller accepts power and income.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattage is power expressed in watts.

clue.text: Church helper's fateful day: months in hospital

indicators.note: in says the day and months are placed inside the word for hospital

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
the Ides of March was the day Julius Caesar was murdered
M is the abbreviation for month or months

explanation.surface: A church helper spends months in hospital after a fateful day.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidesman is an assistant churchwarden who shows people to pews and takes the collection.

clue.text: Possibly copper's sphere of operation

definitions.meaning: copper is one example of a chemical substance in the periodic table
a natural environment, as in being in one's own

explanation.surface: A police officer's beat.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a policeman, but it is the metal; the 's is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is a chemical element, and one's element is the setting where one thrives.

clue.text: Whip restraining leader of riotous mob

indicators.note: restraining says the whip holds in the letter that follows

parts.note: a thong is a leather strip used as a whip

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of riotous

explanation.surface: A whip holds back the ringleader of a rioting mob.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a large crowd of people, a mob.

clue.text: War zone aid, one with companion picking up litter?

definitions.meaning: a battlefield helper carrying wounded soldiers to safety

definitions.text: one with companion picking up litter?
definitions.meaning: a litter is a stretcher, lifted by a pair of carriers rather than rubbish being collected

explanation.surface: A battlefield helper and a pal cleaning up rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Litter looks like rubbish, but it is the old word for a stretcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretcher-bearers carry wounded people in pairs, each holding one end of the litter.

clue.text: It goes round and round and up and down

indicators.note: up and down says the word reads the same both ways in a down light

parts.note: the spinning blade assembly of a helicopter, read here as the word that the reading-both-ways test is applied to

explanation.surface: Something that spins and also moves up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine such as a helicopter.

clue.text: Italian beggars left Arizona oddly, touring Zaire's capital

indicators.note: touring says the shuffled letters travel round Zaire's first letter
oddly says the letters of Arizona are arranged in a strange way
capital means the first letter of Zaire's

explanation.surface: Italian beggars leave Arizona strangely, travelling to Zaire's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts AZARONI (the anagram of ARIZONA, from 'oddly') round Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazzaroni were the poor street beggars and idlers of Naples.

clue.text: Extreme character converting daughter to new form of Buddhism

indicators.note: converting says one letter of the extreme character is swapped for another

parts.note: zed is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An extremist converts their daughter to a new Buddhist sect.
explanation.definitionFit: Zen is a Japanese school of Mahayana Buddhism stressing meditation.

clue.text: German artist's way with English sailors

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A German painter's manner goes down well with English sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born Dada and Surrealist painter.

clue.text: Slightly burn grouse primarily served during function

indicators.note: served during says that letter goes inside the word for function

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letter of the word grouse

explanation.surface: A grouse is served lightly scorched at a formal dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To singe is to scorch the surface or tips of something lightly.

clue.text: Old journalist's fixed stare always taking in Times

indicators.note: taking in says the stare and the word for always together hold the letters for Times

parts.note: a gaze is a long fixed look
e'er is poetic for ever, always
T is times in multiplication, so two Ts are Times

explanation.surface: A veteran reporter stares fixedly at the Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link word; Times is the multiplication sign, not the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazetteer once meant a writer for a gazette, an old word for a newspaper journalist.
